Joining a pen

You need an invite link from someone in the pen and a Mac or Linux computer. It takes about a minute.

Your first computer · How it connects · In practice · More devices · Updating · Leaving · Options

Your first computer

  1. Open your invite link on the computer you want to join. Invites work once and expire after 7 days.
  2. Paste the command it shows into Terminal. It's the same short command for everyone in the pen: 
    $ curl -fsSL https://smith.gate.hogman.network/start | sh
    It asks for your invite link (the page has a button to copy it), downloads hogman-join for your computer, checks it against its published SHA-256, saves it as ~/hogman-join, and runs it. Your link never goes into the command. The script is short enough to read first; the page also shows the same steps by hand.
  3. The page picks the right download for your computer. If you'd rather fetch it yourself, the files are on the same host under /join/dl/, with checksums in SHA256SUMS:
    Mac, Apple siliconhogman-join-Darwin-arm64
    Mac, Intelhogman-join-Darwin-x86_64
    Linux, x86-64hogman-join-Linux-x86_64
    Linux, ARM (Raspberry Pi 4/5, ARM servers)hogman-join-Linux-aarch64
    Windows (untested)hogman-join-windows-amd64.exe
  4. Pick your name when asked: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2 to 32 characters. It's how the pen knows you.
  5. You're in. hogman-join verifies the gate using your OS's built-in HTTPS trust store, checks that your pen's home page loads over HTTPS, sets up your browser proxy, and opens it. Keep the hogman-join file: you'll use it to update, share things, and leave.

On a Mac, two things may pop up. Both are expected.

  • "Allow hogman-join to find devices on local networks?" Either answer works. Allow lets your devices in the same home or office reach each other directly, which is faster. Don't Allow sends that traffic over the internet instead. Nothing on your network is shared with the pen either way.
  • Your Mac's password, once, so your browsers can find the pen's sites. It changes only the automatic proxy setting. If you skip it, hogman-join prints the one setting to change by hand.

Using a VPN (ProtonVPN, Mullvad, or a work VPN)? On macOS, VPN apps override the system automatic proxy setting while connected, so browsers stop seeing pen names even though hogman-join stays connected.

  • Firefox (works today with no extension): set Firefox's built-in Settings → Network Settings → Automatic proxy configuration URL to the http://127.0.0.1:<port>/proxy.pac URL printed by hogman-join. Pen names go straight to hogman-join while ordinary browsing stays on your VPN.
  • Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Firefox extension (developer preview): the companion extension in browser-ext/ is not yet published on the Chrome Web Store or Mozilla Add-ons. Developers can load it manually from browser-ext/dist/ (see browser-ext/README.md; note that Firefox removes temporary add-ons on restart, and Firefox Private Windows send pen names to public DNS unless Run in Private Windows is enabled for the extension).
  • Safari: Apple does not expose proxy APIs to Safari extensions, so pause your VPN while visiting pen sites in Safari.

If it stops part way (DNS not ready, offline), fix what it says and run the same command again. If the stop came before your device joined, the invite is still unused; if after, the rerun sees the device is already in and skips the invite. Either way the link only ever adds this one computer.

Links from before public certificates (carrying fp=) are refused — ask whoever sent the link for a fresh one. Pens created before that release must be recreated.

How it connects

One way, on every computer: a small background connection of its own, running as you (never as administrator), that starts by itself when you log in. It carries HTTPS to the pen's names, and nothing else (if you type an http:// address, the connection itself sends you to HTTPS). Your other networks, your own Tailscale if you have one, and everything else on the computer are left alone.

That's deliberate: a pen is for websites, and anything more is more for an attacker to use. There's no setting for more: see what Hogman deliberately doesn't do.

In practice

Only programs that use the proxy reach the pen. The join tool prints your proxy address (something like http://127.0.0.1:21234) and sets things up:

  • Browsers: on a Mac, the tool sets the automatic proxy setting for you (it never replaces a non-Hogman setting). If you join more than one pen, any pen's proxy.pac routes each pen's own names automatically and updates the Mac setting when you join or leave. On Linux and Windows, set your browser's or desktop's automatic proxy configuration URL to the proxy.pac address it prints (one URL covers every pen you join, though you may need to reload browser proxy settings when adding or leaving a pen). The rules file sends only pen names through their pens.
  • curl and most command-line tools, per command: 
    $ https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21234 curl https://blog.smith.pens.hogman.network
    Don't export it for the whole shell: the proxy refuses everything outside the pen.
  • git, per site: 
    $ git config --global http.https://git.smith.pens.hogman.network/.proxy http://127.0.0.1:21234

More devices

On your pen's home page, press Add a device. You get a one-time link (and a QR code) that works once and expires in an hour. Open it on the other computer and copy the command, as before; the device joins as you. Phones can't join yet; the app is in the works.

To put something in the pen, you don't need another device: see Putting things in your pen.

Updating

$ ./hogman-join update

This downloads the latest hogman-join from your pen's server (or from a host or link you pass: ./hogman-join update 'https://your-pen.gate.hogman.network'), updates this program, updates your pen's installed agent copy and restarts it if it is running, refreshes any cached share binaries on disk from that server (restarting background service-managed shares cleanly while leaving foreground or unmanaged shares running until you restart them), and removes any leftover old Hogman private root certificates from your computer's trust store. On more than one pen? Pick one with --pen ZONE. Use --dry-run to see what would change without touching files.

Before replacing anything on disk, update checks the download's SHA-256 checksum against SHA256SUMS on the same server over the same HTTPS connection. That catches truncated or corrupted downloads and mismatched CDN copies — not a tampered server, which is the same trust model as the first download.

Leaving

$ ./hogman-join leave '<your link>'

This takes down anything you share from this computer, removes any leftover old Hogman root certificate if present, stops the pen's background connection and removes its settings. Your membership stays; the keeper removes members.

Options

--handle NAMEYour name in the pen, instead of being asked.
--hostname NAMEWhat this device is called (default: the computer's name).
--no-serviceRun in the background without starting at login.
--no-system-proxyDon't change the Mac's proxy setting.
--dry-runCheck the link and the pen, change nothing.
--no-openDon't open the home page at the end.
--pen ZONEWhich pen to use with share or update, when on more than one.

Run ./hogman-join --help for the full list.
